title: Windows exchange cancellation fixture never becomes ready within 8 s under parallel load
outcome: Windows exchange cancellation fixture never becomes ready within 8 s under parallel load
acceptance: The failure of task_sync::exchange::tests::windows::task_exchange_windows_cancellation_kills_descendants_and_inherited_pipes ('fixture never became ready', windows.rs:129, an 8 s wait for a grandchild to hold its lock) is diagnosed with available evidence: how the readiness wait is bounded, what the fixture does before readiness, and its measured quiet timing against the failing run's load.

The test passes reliably in full gates under the project's normal concurrent workload without loosening what it proves (cancellation kills descendants and closes inherited pipes); no retry-until-green and no skip.

completion.summary: Windows cancellation fixture now observes readiness while polling the same owned execution; cancellation and future drop preserve descendant and inherited-pipe closure checks. Competing 8s readiness waits use the existing total15s execution watchdog. Bounded secret-safe stage diagnostics and early-error/probe controls added. Historical failure cause remains unproven; quiet timing and one exact-input full PASS establish bounded evidence, not every-load assurance.
